newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Importer demand and dollar short-covering pushed the rand to weaker levels against the U.S. unit in active trade, after it started the day on a firm footing.
The local unit finished at 4.5250/5300 against the dollar from a 4.5100/50 close on Wednesday, after briefly breaking through the key 4.50 level on the downside in early trade.

"There was a big import order below the 4.50 level and with the crosses, like the mark/rand, looking quite healthy, there was more importer demand," a dealer said. "That fuelled the whole run-up again."
Dealers said dollar short-covering also weakened the rand.
"There were a lot of dollars expected to be sold out of Malaysia. The whole of Johannesburg went short on this and the market was caught with its pants down," a dealer said.
The rand touched a day's worst level of 4.5310 during the afternoon, but dealers said some exporter demand above the 4.53 level and rumoured pressure from the Reserve Bank, propped up the local unit.
"Exporters were seen selling above the 4.53 level and the Bank looked like it was there too," a trader said.
Dealers said it was difficult to predict a range for Friday following the currency's erratic moves on Thursday.
"It is very confusing. We started out positive this morning and slipped right back again. But I don't see the rand breaking above the 4.54-4.5450 level tomorrow (Friday)," a dealer said.
Against the crosses the local unit weakened to last trade at 7.0848/0967 from 7.0593/0717 against sterling late on Wednesday and at 0.3379/3384 marks from 0.3386/3391 previously.
On the bond market yields climbed to their worst levels of the day in late trading amid rand jitters and a lack of institutional and foreign involvement, dealers said.
At 1400 GMT the key R150 bond was at 15.210 pct from 15.185 at the same time on Wednesday.
"The rand has not performed as well as people would have liked. But it has also weakened in a tight range which has not done too much damage to the bond market," a dealer said.
Traders said a hoped for boost from the U.S. gilts market did not materialise as the 30-year Treasury bond held fairly steady following the release of weekly jobless claims which came in steady.
New jobless claims for the week totalled 340,000 in line with forecasts. The key U.S. bond was last at 6.83 percent.
Dealers said the keen foreign interest evident over the past two days was lacking on Thursday.
"The overseas guys and local institutions are taking a bit of a rest after the hectic activity of the past couple of days. There is not much going on in our market," one said.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners bought a net 353.96 million rand worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying a net 223.31 million rand on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 5.35 billion rand slightly down from 5.61 billion rand on Tuesday.

On the money market, three-month NCDs rose to trade at between 15.75 and 15.95 percent from between 15.70 to 15.90 percent on Wednesday, while 90-day BAs climbed to a 15.20-15.35 percent band from between 15.15 and 15.30 percent before.

The daily shortage jumped over one billion rand to just below the 10 billion rand level, Reserve Bank figures show. The shortage touched 9.936 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.869 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
